newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chronology of North Korean defection drama.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of North Korean defection drama.

text.p: The departure from China to the Philippines of North Korea's top ideologue on Tuesday is the latest twist in a drama that began when Hwang Jang-yop arrived in Seoul's consulate in Beijing five weeks ago.
The following is a chronology of the events:
Jan 30 - Hwang visits Japan on lecture tour to promote North Korea's ideology of "juche", or self-reliance, which he helped author.
Feb 11 - Hwang arrives in Beijing on his way home.
Feb 12 - Hwang and an aide walk into Seoul consulate seeking political asylum. North Korean cars park outside the diplomatic compound.

Feb 13 - South Korea sends envoy to Beijing to negotiate Hwang's release, but he is rebuffed. North Korea accuses Seoul of kidnapping Hwang. Seoul releases memo it says Hwang wrote expressing his wish to go to Seoul and discuss national reunification.
Feb 14 - South Korean foreign minister Yoo Chong-ha meets his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen in Singapore. Qians says Beijing needs time to investigate Hwang's case.
Feb 15 - Prominent North Korean defector fatally shot outside Seoul, and South Korean authorities say they seeking two suspected Pyongyang hitmen.
Feb 17 - North Korea says if Hwang genuine defector, he is a renegade and will be dismissed.
Feb 19 - Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping dies. Mourning delays talks on Hwang's fate.

Feb 22 - North Korea announces death of powerful defence minister Choe Kwang, a day after revelation that prime minister Kang Song-san has been replaced, adding to fears of political instability in Pyongyang.
March 10 - South Korea says expects breakthrough soon on negotiations with China over Hwang's fate.
March 14 - Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng says conditions "nearly ripe" for solving Hwang problem.
March 18 - Hwang leaves Beijing for the Philippines.
